name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Weber's large financial advantage ($920K vs. negative cash for Bartie)
No polling or expert ratings; markets price Democrats at ~3%
model.rationale: The district's R+12 lean, Weber's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge over a Democratic challenger with essentially no money all point to a comfortable Republican win, and Polymarket prices a Weber win at about 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Weber underperforming his partisan lean, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this Gulf Coast district that leans Republican by about twelve points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding roughly $920,000 on hand, while Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised only about $27,000 and reports negative cash. No outside groups are spending against Weber, and prediction markets give him roughly a 96% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and incumbency. Bartie would need an unusual late shift to put the seat in play; the current evidence points to a solid Weber win.
